comparison.objective: Wafer task identifies, flips, orients, centers, and vacuum-selects the correct wafer using tweezers; candidate commissions and locks an adjustable damper through impact trials.
comparison.physical_skill: Wafer task emphasizes tweezer pickup, fragile edge-safe handling, bimanual handoff/reorientation, precision placement, and toggle actuation. Candidate emphasizes recessed hex-key engagement, counterholding, setscrew and collar manipulation, tightening-force control, and iterative tuning from observed motion.
comparison.success_condition: Wafer: correct wafer face-down within 3°, center within 2 mm, flat within 2°, vacuum toggle on, tools withdrawn, with zero-score contamination/drop/wrong-wafer events. Candidate: physical unlock-adjust-relock plus two safe stops meeting energy, velocity, and stroke constraints with no drift or damage. Candidate lacks numeric rebound, overload, locking-torque, and drift thresholds; wafer vacuum and tape adhesion are not physically simulated.
comparison.reason: Fragile part identification, reorientation, and precision mounting does not test mechanical setting retention or adjustment based on repeated dynamic impacts. Shared fine manipulation and control actuation do not make the tested abilities equivalent.
